sound: small ya, which joins to the preceding sign and makes one mora with it
components: a small や-shaped sweep curling into a hook on the right
a short tick at the top
a small descender crossing the sweep
strokeOrder: begin on the left and sweep right, curling clockwise into the hook
lift; add the short tick at the top
lift; draw the descender from the upper left down across the sweep to the lower right
strokeOrderNote: Sirgazil's 28-frame や animation supplies the three-run order, sweep first and descender last; KanjiVG's 03083 file holds the same three strokes in the same order for U+3083 itself, and Unicode names U+3083 HIRAGANA LETTER SMALL YA, so the movement is fitted to the smaller bundled glyph exactly as small ゅ is fitted from ゆ.

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sirgazil, Hiragana や stroke order animation.gif, hiragana や, 28 frames, 2.8 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009); KanjiVG kanji/03083.svg, three stroke paths in the same order; the Unicode Standard names U+3083 HIRAGANA LETTER SMALL YA
strokeOrderSource.variation: The CC0 animation draws full-size や in three pen-down runs with two lifts: the long sweep and its hook first, then the short tick, then the descender. KanjiVG records U+3083 with the same three strokes in the same order. Unicode separately identifies U+3083 as small ya. This learner path therefore preserves the source's three-run movement while scaling and fitting it to the bundled Noto Sans JP small ゃ outline; the cited animation demonstrates や rather than a separately animated ゃ, so the size adaptation is explicit rather than presented as independent handwriting evidence.

notes: A yōon sign: it does not take a beat of its own but fuses with the sign before it, so ち + ゃ is one mora cha, as in おちゃ, tea. Its full-size twin や takes a beat of its own.
